I give up. I read the file and the statement is a real combinatorics result (IMO Shortlist 2011 C6), not a formal shortcut. The hypotheses are an arbitrary binary periodic word with minimal period N > 2^n, and the conclusion needs n distinct nonempty ubiquitous words.

Ubiquitous here means U is both left- and right-special, i.e. a nonempty bispecial factor. A proof would need the factor-complexity facts for periodic words (Morse–Hedlund), the right-special counts, and a bispecial counting argument that gives n distinct nonempty bispecials. Formalizing that over `ℤ → Fin 2` with the `Σ k, Fin k → Fin 2` encoding, with no Mathlib sources to consult, is far beyond what I can finish here. I have not modified `/work/combi_imosl_2011_c6.lean`, so the `sorry` is still in place.

I give up.
